name: M64/60 CP1 piston with closed cooling gallery, F0 twin

coordinate_system.origin: geometric center of the piston's cylindrical F0 envelope
coordinate_system.axes: Z along the cylinder axis toward the chamber, X along the piston pin axis, Y completes the right-handed frame

interfaces.acceptance_rule: The measured diametral clearance stays within the approved map cold, hot and under piston tilt, with no seizure or oil-film breakdown.
The machined grooves, clearances, contacts and coatings meet the ring definition and the approved limits for flutter, wear, temperature and blow-by.
Contact pressure, deformation, fatigue and pin-boss pull-out stay below the qualified allowables over the whole load history.
The kinematic and thermomechanical envelope keeps the approved piston-to-head and piston-to-valve clearances across tolerances and overspeed.
The depowdered and sealed gallery captures the jet, drains the oil and meets the temperature and pressure limits demonstrated by correlated CFD, CT and proof testing.

known_limits: The piston envelope, skirt, crown, pin bosses, grooves and gallery are independent F0 assumptions, not Porsche or MAHLE surfaces.
The published 100 mm engine bore defines neither the finished cylinder diameter, nor the piston gauge diameter, nor the running clearance.
The four interface contexts remain without geometry until the exact parts and their tolerances are established.

The analyses now include a full-part LPBF slicing, an isolated SimReady asset and six linear/sequential CalculiX cases on the sound master; no nonlinear FEA with contacts, CFD/VOF, hot fatigue, Omniverse assembly simulation or PhysicsNeMo correlation is complete.

The hot CalculiX case at 2.5 mm gives 323.46 MPa at p95 and a ratio of 0.918 against the room-temperature CP1 reference; this unfavorable comparison rejects the F0 without constituting a hot allowable.
The PicoGK screening was indeed run on six F0 variants, but it selects no design: the target mechanical margin and manifold integrity fail.
The Porsche/Mahle/Trumpf precedent defines a modern development method, not a validation transferable to the M64/60.
No manufacturing, installation or engine start-up is authorized.
